clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 20s presented with a 4-month history of progressive swelling and pruritus localized to the right posterior scalp (parieto-occipital region). Clinical examination identified two distinct lesions: a 12 mm subcutaneous mobile tender cystic lesion with intact skin and an 11 mm erythematous lesion with irregular borders and brown discoloration. Ultrasound imaging revealed two adjacent hypoechoic lesions in the parietal region (largest 10×8 mm) resembling epidermoid cysts. An excisional biopsy of the second lesion was performed under local anesthesia and submitted for histopathological analysis. Histopathology revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma on H&E staining. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis with patchy epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) staining of the apical aspect of pseudo-glandular cysts and diffuse pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) positive staining. PET-CT staging showed no fluorodeoxyglucose uptake or hypermetabolic activity, indicating absence of distant metastases. Both lesions were subsequently completely excised surgically under local anesthesia with reconstruction using a local rotational flap of adjacent scalp tissue.
